formulas.formula: Simple bookkeeping for your small business: income, expenses, profit, taxes and invoices.
1. Setup: your business name, the year, how much to set aside for taxes and the mileage rate.
2. Still on Setup: name your income and expense categories, and how much of each expense is deductible.
3. Transactions: log every sale and expense (date, category, amount). Type fills in by itself.
4. Monthly P&L and Profit & Loss: income, expenses and profit by month, quarter and year.
5. Taxes: estimated tax to set aside each quarter, with due dates, plus sales tax collected vs. paid.
6. Mileage Log: business trips and the mileage deduction.
7. Invoices: who owes you, what's overdue, and what's been paid.
8. Dashboard: your whole year at a glance.
Money you pay yourself isn't a business expense: its deductible % is 0 and it's left out of profit.
100% for most expenses, 50% for meals or a phone you also use personally.
Move your tax set-aside to a separate savings account each month.
Note where each receipt is saved (a folder or photo) in the Notes column.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: profit, paid, or money in.
Red: something to check (a typo, an unknown category, an overdue invoice, a loss).
Tax figures are estimates to help you plan, not tax advice. Check with a tax professional.
Thank you for your purchase! Here's to a profitable year.

Set these once. Category names here feed the drop-downs on Transactions and every report.
% of taxable profit (type 25 or 25%). Ask a tax pro for your number.
Per business mile (check the current rate).
Your own pay: not a business expense (0%).
Every sale and every expense, one row each. Pick a category and the Type fills in. Amounts are before sales tax; put any sales tax you collected in its own column.
Income and expenses by category and month, from Transactions. Owner draw (0% deductible) isn't counted as an expense.
Your profit & loss statement by quarter and for the year.
Estimated income tax to set aside each quarter, and sales tax collected vs. sent in. Estimates only: check your numbers with a tax professional.
Log each business trip. Round trip = Yes doubles the miles. Commuting from home to a regular workplace usually doesn't count.
Track every invoice. When one is paid, add the date here AND log the payment on Transactions as income.
